title: Dates, Times and Culture
summary: Getting time and formatting right in .NET - DateTime and its Kind, DateTimeOffset for moments, DateOnly and TimeOnly for calendar values, TimeSpan and date arithmetic, time zones with TimeZoneInfo, TimeProvider for testable code, and CultureInfo for numbers and dates that look right in every country and parse the same everywhere.

cards.a:
UTC has no daylight saving jumps and is the same everywhere

Local times repeat or skip an hour at daylight saving changes and differ between places, so UTC values compare and sort correctly. Convert to local time only to display.

cards.q: Which culture should a CSV file your program writes and reads use for numbers?
cards.a:
`CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`, so the file reads back the same on any computer

With the current culture a German computer writes 1,5, which breaks the commas of a CSV and reads back differently elsewhere. The invariant culture is fixed.

cards.q: A TimeSpan of 200 minutes: what are Hours and TotalHours?
cards.a:
3 and 3.33

Hours is the whole hours part; TotalHours is the full length expressed in hours.
